# Suplex

> Suplex runs coordinated coding agents against your repositories. External agents read and create tasks through OAuth MCP or the authenticated Agent API.

## Authorization

The remote MCP endpoint uses OAuth 2.1 browser approval. The Agent API uses a paired-agent bearer credential. Both methods bind one external-agent identity to one company and its granted projects.

## Public discovery

- GET /llms.txt (none): Plain-text overview of this deployment for machine readers.
- GET /.well-known/suplex/api-catalog.json (none): This catalog.
- GET /.well-known/suplex/agent-skills.json (none): Agent skill and client discovery index.
- GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp (none): OAuth metadata for the MCP resource.
- GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource (none): OAuth metadata for clients that use root discovery.
- GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server (none): OAuth authorization server metadata.

## Pairing

- POST /api/agent/pairing/exchange (pairing code): Exchange a one-time pairing code for a scoped agent credential. The code is single use.

## Runtime API

Read /api/agent/openapi.json after pairing. That document is authoritative; this file is a map.

- POST /mcp (OAuth bearer): The Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint.
- GET /api/agent/openapi.json (agent credential): The authoritative OpenAPI 3.0.3 contract for the runtime routes. Read it after pairing.
- GET /api/agent/capabilities (agent credential): The commands this deployment accepts and the commands it does not.
- GET /api/agent/me (agent credential): The agent identity and the projects granted to it.
- GET /api/agent/workflows (agent credential): List workflow records for a granted project and whether task creation permits each one.
- GET /api/agent/templates (agent credential): List task templates for a granted project and whether task creation permits each one.
- GET /api/agent/tasks (agent credential): List tasks in the agent's currently granted projects. Filter by pull request number, source branch, or title substring. HTTP defaults to the full view; MCP suplex_list_tasks defaults to summary and accepts view=full.
- POST /api/agent/tasks (agent credential): Create a backlog task, or a queued task with queue true. dryRun validates without writing state. An idempotency key is necessary unless dryRun is true. A queued task starts by itself only when every prerequisite is complete. Task input errors include project_not_found, dependency_not_found, root_profile_not_found, worker_profile_not_found, advisor_profile_not_found, source_issue_rejected, source_pull_request_rejected, source_branch_rejected, workflow_not_found, workflow_not_permitted, template_not_found, and template_not_permitted. They include field, value, and reason.
- GET /api/agent/tasks/{taskId} (agent credential): Read one task. Send the ETag in If-None-Match to poll conditionally.
- PUT /api/agent/tasks/{taskId}/dependencies (agent credential): Replace the prerequisites of a task, shown as Blocked by. Task input errors include project_not_found, dependency_not_found, root_profile_not_found, worker_profile_not_found, advisor_profile_not_found, source_issue_rejected, source_pull_request_rejected, source_branch_rejected, workflow_not_found, workflow_not_permitted, template_not_found, and template_not_permitted. They include field, value, and reason.
- POST /api/agent/tasks/{taskId}/commands (agent credential): Apply one lifecycle command with the current revision and an idempotency key. start_task queues a task and disarm_task returns it to the manual backlog.

## Clients

- MCP: connect a Streamable HTTP client to `/mcp` and complete OAuth browser approval.
- MCP stdio: run the advanced local bridge with `suplex mcp`.
- HTTP: send `Authorization: Bearer <credential>` to the runtime routes.

## Administration

OAuth connections, pairing codes, credential rotation, revocation, and project grants appear on the Agents page. An administrator controls them.

## Notes

- Suplex conceals tasks that the caller cannot read. Denied and missing tasks both answer 404 with resource_not_found.
- Human answers remain unavailable to paired agents. The runtime API exposes delivery and merge commands only when capabilities reports them. Suplex can perform delivery for a task's configured target, including a merge after review, without an agent command.
- MCP exposes task lifecycle commands only. It does not expose runtime delivery or merge commands. Human answers remain unavailable to paired agents. Suplex can perform delivery for a task's configured target, including a merge after review, without an agent command.
